Test Whether Classifier Features Affect the Outcome Directly

Source: R/exclusion.R
exclusion_test.Rd

The classifier behind the probabilities must use features beyond the controls, and these features must affect the outcome only through the group. If an extra feature has its own effect on the outcome, the model of soft_lm() is misspecified and the estimate is biased. On labelled data this is testable: exclusion_test() regresses the outcome on the observed group, the controls and the extra features by least squares, and reports a robust Wald test that the coefficients of the extra features are zero.

Usage

exclusion_test(
  formula,
  group,
  extra,
  data,
  reference = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  cluster = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_exclusion'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

formula

[mandatory] (formula) A formula outcome ~ controls, as in soft_lm().

group

[mandatory] (vector or character) Observed category labels: a vector or a column name of data.

extra

[mandatory] (formula or character) The classifier features that are not controls: a one-sided formula or a character vector of column names.

data

[mandatory] (data.frame) A data frame of labelled observations.

reference

[optional] (character) Reference level of group. NULL uses the first level (default: NULL).

weights

[optional] (numeric, character or formula) Observation weights (default: NULL).

cluster

[optional] (vector, character or formula) Cluster identifier for cluster-robust standard errors. Without clusters the standard errors are HC1, with the factor \(n / (n - p)\) for \(p\) regressors; with clusters they are CR1, with the factors \((n - 1) / (n - p)\) and \(G / (G - 1)\) for \(G\) clusters (default: NULL).

x

[mandatory] (softcats_exclusion) Result of exclusion_test().

digits

[optional] (integer) Number of significant digits to print (default: 3).

...

[optional] Not used.

Value

An object of class softcats_exclusion with the Wald statistic, its degrees of freedom df, the p.value, the coefficients of the extra features and nobs. The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

The test is linear in the extra features and in the terms of formula. Add transformations to formula or extra to test other forms of dependence.

Examples

# Example: The classifier feature z affects the outcome directly
d <- sim_softcats(n = 3000, K = 2, direct_effect = 0.5, seed = 8)
lab <- d[d$labelled, ]
exclusion_test(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, group = "group", extra = ~ z, data = lab)
#> Direct-effect test for the classifier features (590 labelled observations)
#> 
#>  term estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>     z    0.432     0.046      9.39 6.21e-21
#> 
#> Wald chi-squared = 88.1 on 1 df, p < 1e-04 (HC1 standard errors)
#> The extra features predict the outcome beyond the group and the controls,
#> which violates the exclusion restriction of soft_lm(). Move them into the
#> controls or use a classifier without them.
